# EA Azure DevOps Practices

**← Back to [EAP Home](../README.md) • [Foundation](./README.md)**

---

> This document provides specific guidance for Enterprise Architects (EAs) on how to use Azure DevOps (ADO) to manage architecture work, track architecture initiatives, and collaborate with product engineering and implementation teams. This guidance applies to all EA roles at Gainwell:
> - **Domain EAs**: Organized by architecture domains (Business, Application, Data, Infrastructure, Security) providing enterprise-wide guidance and governance
> - **Product EAs**: Supporting Gainwell product engineering teams
> - **DDI EAs**: Supporting state healthcare implementation programs (Design, Deliver, Implement)
>
> All EA work is considered non-technical and focuses on strategy, governance, stakeholder engagement, and documentation. For general work item states and workflow, see [Work Item Management](work-item-management.md).

### 1.1 EA Responsibilities

Enterprise Architects use Azure DevOps to manage and track:

- **Strategic Planning**: Business capability assessments, operating model design, technology roadmaps
- **Architecture Research**: Requirements analysis, stakeholder assessments, vendor evaluations, feasibility studies
- **Documentation**: Creating and maintaining business architecture artifacts, capability models, process maps, standards
- **Governance**: Architecture reviews, compliance assessments (MECT, HIPAA, etc.), standards enforcement
- **Stakeholder Engagement**: Facilitating workshops, requirements gathering, design sessions, status reporting
- **Knowledge Management**: Maintaining the reference architecture, best practices, lessons learned
page_texts.5:
[foundation/ea-ado-practices.md#12-ea-vs-product-engineering--implementation-team-workflows]

### 1.2 EA vs Product Engineering & Implementation Team Workflows

| Aspect | EA Workflow | Engineering & Implementation Team Workflow |
| ------ | ----------- | ------------------------- |
| **Primary Focus** | Strategy, architecture, governance, standards | Product development, delivery, implementation, configuration |
| **Work Duration** | Variable (days to weeks) | Sprint-aligned (1-2 weeks) |
| **Work Items** | Epics, Features, User Stories | Features, Stories, Tasks, Bugs |
| **Board View** | Portfolio/program view | Team-specific board |
| **Success Metrics** | Stakeholder alignment, compliance, risk mitigation | Velocity, burndown, completion |
| **Collaboration** | Multi-team, cross-functional, advisory | Team-focused, delivery-oriented |

[foundation/ea-ado-practices.md#21-architecture-research--analysis]

### 2.1 Architecture Research & Analysis

**Work Item Type**: Epic or Feature

**When to Use**:
- Business capability assessments
- Current state / future state analysis
- Vendor solution evaluations
- Feasibility studies
- Requirements analysis
- Stakeholder impact assessments

**Key Fields**:
- **Business Question**: What are we trying to understand?
- **Success Criteria**: How will we measure success?
- **Options Evaluated**: What alternatives were considered?
- **Recommendation**: Final decision and rationale

**Examples**:
- **Domain EA**: "Assess Enterprise Data Architecture Maturity Across Gainwell"
- **Product EA**: "Evaluate Payment Processing Architecture Options for Product Roadmap"
- **DDI EA**: "Analyze Current State Eligibility System Capabilities - State of Ohio"
page_texts.8:
[foundation/ea-ado-practices.md#22-architecture-documentation]

### 2.2 Architecture Documentation

**Work Item Type**: User Story

**When to Use**:
- Creating business architecture artifacts (capability models, value streams, process maps)
- Documenting architecture decisions and rationale
- Writing standards and guidelines
- Maintaining reference architecture content
- Creating stakeholder presentation materials

**Key Fields**:
- **Documentation Type**: Business Architecture, Decision Record, Standard, Guide, Presentation
- **Target Audience**: Who will use this documentation? (Enterprise teams, product teams, state stakeholders, executives)
- **Related Work**: Links to dependent decisions or initiatives
- **Review Status**: Draft, Under Review, Approved

**Examples**:
- **Domain EA**: "Document Enterprise Integration Reference Architecture"
- **Product EA**: "Create Claims Processing Capability Model for Product Portfolio"
- **DDI EA**: "Develop State MMIS Integration Architecture Overview for California Stakeholders"
page_texts.9:
[foundation/ea-ado-practices.md#23-standards-and-guidelines]

### 2.3 Standards and Guidelines

**Work Item Type**: Feature or User Story

**When to Use**:
- Defining architectural standards and principles
- Establishing governance frameworks
- Creating design guidelines
- Setting compliance requirements
- Documenting best practices

**Key Fields**:
- **Standard/Guideline Name**: Clear, descriptive name
- **Scope**: What does this apply to? (business units, programs, systems)
- **Enforcement**: How is compliance ensured? (reviews, checkpoints, audits)
- **Adoption Plan**: Communication and rollout strategy

**Examples**:
- **Domain EA**: "Establish Enterprise Data Governance Framework for All Gainwell Products and Programs"
- **Product EA**: "Define Product Architecture Review Checkpoint Process"
- **DDI EA**: "Create State Implementation Architecture Documentation Standards"
page_texts.10:
[foundation/ea-ado-practices.md#24-architecture-reviews--assessments]

### 2.4 Architecture Reviews & Assessments

**Work Item Type**: User Story

**When to Use**:
- Pre-implementation architecture reviews
- Design reviews for major initiatives
- Compliance assessments (MECT, HIPAA, state requirements)
- Vendor solution evaluations
- Post-implementation evaluations

**Key Fields**:
- **Review Type**: Design Review, Compliance Assessment, Vendor Evaluation, Checkpoint Review
- **Artifacts Reviewed**: Business requirements, architecture diagrams, process flows, compliance documentation
- **Findings**: Issues, risks, or gaps identified
- **Recommendations**: Actions required or suggested improvements

**Tracking Review Decisions**:
- Document approval decision in comments with `@mentions` to notify stakeholders
- Use standard User Story states: "Under Review" (in progress), "Done" (approved), "Blocked" (needs rework)
- Tag with review outcome: `approved`, `conditional-approval`, or `needs-rework`

**Examples**:
- **Domain EA**: "Enterprise Security Architecture Assessment for Cloud Migration Strategy"
- **Product EA**: "Product Release Architecture Review - Provider Portal v3.0"
- **DDI EA**: "MECT Compliance Assessment - Phase 2 Ohio MMIS Implementation"
page_texts.11:
[foundation/ea-ado-practices.md#25-architecture-modernization--risk-management]

### 2.5 Architecture Modernization & Risk Management

**Work Item Type**: Epic or Feature

**When to Use**:
- Tracking known architectural risks or gaps
- Planning modernization initiatives
- Managing legacy system dependencies
- Addressing compliance deficiencies
- Business process improvements

**Key Fields**:
- **Risk/Gap Category**: Process, System, Compliance, Integration, Business Capability
- **Impact**: Risk to program success, state operations, or compliance
- **Affected Systems/Processes**: What is impacted?
- **Remediation Plan**: How to address
- **Priority**: Based on risk, compliance requirements, and business value

**Examples**:
- **Domain EA**: "Remediate Enterprise-Wide API Security Gaps Across Product Portfolio"
- **Product EA**: "Modernize Member Portal Authentication Architecture"
- **DDI EA**: "Address Legacy Interface Gaps for State Federal Reporting Requirements - Texas"
page_texts.12:
[foundation/ea-ado-practices.md#26-cross-program-initiatives]

### 2.6 Cross-Program Initiatives

**Work Item Type**: Epic

**When to Use**:
- Security or compliance initiatives affecting multiple programs
- Governance framework implementations
- Organization-wide process improvements
- Enterprise-wide standards adoption
- Multi-system integration efforts

**Key Fields**:
- **Affected Programs/Systems**: Which programs or teams are impacted?
- **Dependencies**: External dependencies or prerequisites
- **Coordination Plan**: How will programs collaborate?
- **Success Metrics**: How to measure progress and adoption?

**Examples**:
- **Domain EA**: "Implement Enterprise-Wide Cloud Architecture Standards Across All Gainwell Products"
- **Product EA**: "Establish Shared Integration Platform for Product Portfolio"
- **DDI EA**: "Standardize State Implementation Architecture Approach Across All DDI Contracts"
page_texts.13:
[foundation/ea-ado-practices.md#27-stakeholder-engagement--facilitation]

### 2.7 Stakeholder Engagement & Facilitation

**Work Item Type**: User Story

**When to Use**:
- Facilitating workshops and design sessions
- Stakeholder interviews and requirements gathering
- Presenting architecture recommendations to executives, product leadership, or state officials
- Conducting training or knowledge transfer sessions
- Status reporting and program updates

**Key Fields**:
- **Session Type**: Workshop, Interview, Presentation, Training, Status Meeting
- **Attendees**: Key stakeholders participating
- **Objectives**: What outcomes are expected?
- **Deliverables**: What will be produced? (requirements document, decisions made, presentation materials)
- **Follow-up Actions**: Next steps identified

**Examples**:
- **Domain EA**: "Present Enterprise Reference Architecture to Gainwell Leadership"
- **Product EA**: "Facilitate Product Roadmap Architecture Planning with Engineering Leadership"
- **DDI EA**: "Present State MMIS Architecture Strategy to State Project Director - Pennsylvania"

[foundation/ea-ado-practices.md#31-recommended-board-setup]

### 3.1 Recommended Board Setup

**EA Portfolio Board**:

Azure DevOps User Stories support the following states (see [Work Item Management](work-item-management.md)):
- **New**: Default state for new work items
- **Backlog**: Refined and prioritized, not yet committed
- **Ready**: Committed for current iteration
- **In Progress**: Active work underway
- **Under Review**: EA work pending stakeholder approval or peer review
- **Blocked**: Work stopped due to dependencies
- **Done**: Work completed and accepted

**EA Board Column Configuration**:
- **Columns**: New → Backlog → Ready → In Progress → Under Review → Done
- **Swimlanes**: By architecture domain (Business, Application, Data, Infrastructure, Security) or business area
- **Card Fields**: Business value, affected systems/programs, assigned EA, iteration

**EA Backlog Configuration**:
- Group by: Epic → Feature → User Story
- Filter: Show only EA-owned work items
- Sort by: Strategic priority or WSJF
page_texts.16:
[foundation/ea-ado-practices.md#32-ea-specific-queries]

### 3.2 EA-Specific Queries

Recommended saved queries for EAs:

1. **My Architecture Work**
   - All work items assigned to EA
   - State: Not Done
   - Sort by: Priority

2. **Pending Architecture Reviews**
   - Work Item Type: User Story
   - Tags: architecture-review
   - State: New, Active

3. **Active Standards/Guidelines**
   - Work Item Type: Feature, User Story
   - Tags: standard, guideline, governance
   - State: In Progress

4. **Architecture Risks & Gaps**
   - Work Item Type: Epic, Feature
   - Tags: risk, gap, compliance
   - Sort by: Priority

5. **Cross-Program Initiatives**
   - Work Item Type: Epic
   - Tags: cross-program, enterprise-initiative
   - State: Not Done

[foundation/ea-ado-practices.md#33-ea-dashboard-widgets]

### 3.3 EA Dashboard Widgets

Recommended widgets for EA dashboard:

- **Work Items by State**: Track EA work progress
- **Assigned to Me**: Personal work view
- **Architecture Risks & Gaps**: Filtered query showing risk items requiring attention
- **Review Queue**: Items tagged with architecture-review
- **Completion Trends**: Architecture work completed over time
- **Compliance Status**: Track MECT, HIPAA, and federal compliance activities
- **Custom Markdown**: Links to key documentation (business models, standards, decisions)

[foundation/ea-ado-practices.md#41-linking-to-architecture-decisions]

### 4.1 Linking to Architecture Decisions

**Best Practice**: Link work items to architecture decision documentation for traceability

**Link Type**: Related

**In Work Item Description**:
```markdown
### Architecture Decision
[Decision: Enterprise API Management Strategy](../decisions/application/api-management-strategy.md)

### Rationale
[Brief explanation of why this decision was made and key factors considered]
```

**Examples of Decision Documentation**:
- Enterprise architecture strategy decisions (Domain EA)
- Product design and architecture decisions (Product EA)
- State implementation approach decisions (DDI EA)
- Compliance and governance decisions
page_texts.20:
[foundation/ea-ado-practices.md#42-linking-to-architecture-artifacts]

### 4.2 Linking to Architecture Artifacts

**Best Practice**: Reference architecture artifacts (business models, process flows, capability maps) when work relates to or implements them

**Link Type**: Related

**Tags**: Include artifact type (e.g., `capability-model`, `process-map`, `architecture-diagram`)

**In Work Item Description**:
```markdown
### Related Architecture Artifacts
- [Enterprise Data Architecture Reference Model](../foundation/reference-architecture.md)
- [Claims Processing Product Capability Model](../business-portfolio/payment-integrity-solutions/claims-capability-model.md)
- [State MMIS Integration Architecture Overview - Ohio](../decisions/application/ohio-mmis-integration.md)
```
page_texts.21:
[foundation/ea-ado-practices.md#43-linking-to-standards--guidelines]

### 4.3 Linking to Standards & Guidelines

**Best Practice**: Link compliance and standards work to governance documentation

**Link Type**: Related

**In Work Item Description**:
```markdown
### Applicable Standards & Guidelines
- [Enterprise Cloud Architecture Standards](../standards/infrastructure/cloud-standards.md)
- [Product Architecture Review Process](../governance/processes/product-architecture-review.md)
- [State Implementation Architecture Guidelines](../governance/processes/ddi-architecture-guidelines.md)
```
page_texts.22:
[foundation/ea-ado-practices.md#44-linking-to-business-initiatives]

### 4.4 Linking to Business Initiatives

**Best Practice**: Connect architecture work to business value and strategic initiatives

**Link Types**:
- **Parent**: When EA work supports a larger business initiative (Epic)
- **Related**: When EA work enables or influences business initiatives
- **Dependency**: When business work depends on architecture deliverables

**Example Scenarios**:
- **Domain EA**: Enterprise data governance standards (User Story) is a **child** of Enterprise Data Strategy (Epic)
- **Product EA**: Product architecture review (User Story) is a **child** of Product Release 4.0 (Feature)
- **DDI EA**: State architecture assessment (User Story) is a **child** of Ohio MMIS Implementation (Epic)
- EA compliance review (User Story) has a **dependency** on Business Requirements Completion (Feature)
- EA standards documentation (User Story) is **related** to multiple implementation Features across programs

[foundation/ea-ado-practices.md#51-working-with-implementation-teams]

### 5.1 Working with Implementation Teams

**Advisory Role**:
- **Domain EAs**: Provide enterprise-wide guidance, establish standards, conduct governance reviews
- **Product EAs**: Partner with product engineering teams, guide product roadmap, review product designs
- **DDI EAs**: Support state implementation teams, ensure compliance, guide state-specific architecture

**EA Engagement with Teams**:
- Create parent Features/Epics that teams link Stories to
- Use @mentions to request EA guidance on Stories
- Schedule architecture reviews and checkpoints as User Stories assigned to EA
- Provide design guidance and clarification on business requirements

**Review Process**:
1. Implementation team creates Story requiring EA input
2. Team adds `architecture-review` tag and assigns to EA
3. EA reviews requirements, design, and approach; provides feedback in comments
4. EA updates state to "Under Review" during evaluation
5. Upon completion, EA either:
   - Moves to "Done" if approved (with approval noted in comments)
   - Moves to "Blocked" if issues must be resolved first (with detailed feedback)
   - Returns to "Backlog" or "Ready" with conditional approval and recommendations
6. Team proceeds with implementation or addresses EA feedback
page_texts.25:
[foundation/ea-ado-practices.md#52-architecture-governance-workflow]

### 5.2 Architecture Governance Workflow

**Standard Governance Flow**:

```
New Initiative or Requirements (Epic/Feature)
    ↓
EA Analysis & Research (User Stories)
    ↓
Create Architecture Artifacts (User Stories)
    (Business models, diagrams, decision documentation)
    ↓
Architecture Review / Stakeholder Approval (User Story)
    ↓
Document Finalization (State: Done)
    ↓
Stakeholder Communication & Handoff (User Stories)
    ↓
Implementation Tracking (Feature)
```
page_texts.26:
[foundation/ea-ado-practices.md#53-portfolio-level-tracking]

### 5.3 Portfolio-Level Tracking

**Portfolio Management**:
- Use **Epics** for major architecture initiatives spanning multiple teams
- Use **Features** to break down initiatives into team-specific efforts
- Create **Delivery Plans** to visualize cross-team architecture work
- Use **Dependencies** to track architectural blockers

---
page_texts.28:
[foundation/ea-ado-practices.md#61-architecture-work-metrics]

### 6.1 Architecture Work Metrics

Track these metrics to demonstrate EA value:

- **Architecture Review Throughput**: Reviews and assessments completed per sprint
- **Architecture Documentation**: Business models, process flows, and decisions documented
- **Standards Compliance**: % of initiatives meeting architecture standards
- **Stakeholder Engagement**: Number of workshops, design sessions, and reviews conducted
- **EA Work Velocity**: Architecture user stories and deliverables completed
- **Risk Mitigation**: Architecture risks identified and addressed
page_texts.29:
[foundation/ea-ado-practices.md#62-compliance-tracking]

### 6.2 Compliance Tracking

Use queries and tags to track:
- MECT, HIPAA, and federal compliance reviews completed
- Standards violations or gaps identified
- Remediation work in progress
- Audit findings and certification requirements addressed
page_texts.30:
[foundation/ea-ado-practices.md#63-architecture-risks--gaps-visibility]

### 6.3 Architecture Risks & Gaps Visibility

Report on architecture risks and gaps using:
- Total risk/gap items in backlog
- Issues by category (compliance, integration, process, capability)
- Resolution rate and trend
- High-priority risks requiring immediate attention
